title: SMEs, Regional Headquarters and Workforce Averting Side Effects of US-China Trade Standoff
what_it_is: SMEs, Regional Headquarters and Workforce Averting Side Effects of US-China Trade Standoff

sections.label: SMEs and US-China trade standoff
sections.summary: Asked how Singapore-based SMEs, Regional HQs, MNCs and the workforce can protect themselves from a US-China trade standoff and how innovation helps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry how Singapore-based SMEs, Regional HQs, MNCs and the workforce can protect themselves from the side effects of a US-China trade standoff and how can capitalising on innovation help these organisations overcome such side effects.

sections.label: Diversifying markets, supply chains, FTAs
sections.summary: MTI and economic agencies will continue diversifying markets, supply chains, product mix and the portfolio of FTAs so companies can access growing markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To manage the uncertainties ahead of us, which may take quite a while to settle down, we should continuously diversify our markets, our supply chains and our product mix.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For the diversification of the markets, we must always remember that there are still many parts of the world that are experiencing strong and positive growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And this is the reason why the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), with the economic agencies, will continue to diversify our portfolio of free trade agreements (FTAs), both in terms of the number of FTAs and the quality of FTAs, in order for our companies to access the markets around the world, especially those with strong and positive growth.

sections.label: Sectors down and up
sections.summary: Some sectors such as electronics, precision engineering and wholesale and retail trade are down, while information and communications, biomedical and professional services are up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is how we have approached the situation over the last many years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And if we look at the numbers today, while some sectors like the electronics, precision engineering and wholesale trade and retail are down, there are also sectors like the information and communications sector, biomedical sector and professional services sector that are still up.

sections.label: Scale-up Singapore management training
sections.summary: In the Scale-up Singapore rollout, training focused on the management team's envisioning and change management before workers' training was discussed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, in the recent rollout of the Scale-up Singapore initiative, we did not focus just on the workers' training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We focused on the training of the management team by getting the entire management team to come in, do their envisioning exercise, do their change management exercises together as a team, before we even talked about workers' training.

sections.label: Invest in innovation and training
sections.summary: Continue investing in innovation, building real capabilities rather than capacities, and training both workers and the management team.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Continue to invest in innovation and build real capabilities and not just capacities, and focus on the training not just of the workers but of the management team.

sections.label: FTAs cover Singapore trade
sections.summary: More than 90% of Singapore's trade is already covered by existing FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, for Singapore, more than 90% of all our trade is already covered by the existing FTAs.

sections.label: Post-Brexit UK agreement
sections.summary: Singapore is working with the UK on a short form agreement to continue current arrangements post-Brexit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Corollary to that, on Brexit, we are working with the United Kingdom (UK) administration to see how we can, post-Brexit, have a short form agreement that will essentially continue the current arrangements that we have with the UK as part of the European Union.

sections.label: Leveraging strengths for 600 million market
sections.summary: The opportunity is to work together and leverage each other's strengths to have a 600 million market as a hinterland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our opportunity is how we can work together to bring these different strengths together, to leverage on one another's strengths, so that we can have a 600 million market as a hinterland, rather than depending on ourselves individually.
